scope: Bounded source/assertion audit of ISO 32000-2:2020 with EC3: §§11.3.3–11.3.8 (basic composite, blending space, blend modes, alpha, shape/opacity), §§11.4.4, 11.4.5, 11.4.7, 11.4.8 (group formulas/isolation/page group), and §11.6.4.4 (constant shape and opacity). This is not a clause-wide or all-backend certification.

source_locations.definition: physical p.405 gives Cr=(1−αs/αr)Cb +(αs/αr)((1−αb)Cs+αb B(Cb,Cs)); Table 133 continues on physical p.406 / printed p.391.
Supported blending-space families, per-component arithmetic and conversion/complement rules; exact list additionally continued beyond the opening page.
Mode formula tables and nonseparable Lum/Sat/ClipColor/SetLum/SetSat definitions.

source_locations.topic: §11.3.6–.8 alpha, source/result shape-opacity, basic formula summary
source_locations.definition: General shape/opacities and independent basic compositing computation summary.
Group function, non-isolated non-knockout formula, backdrop removal and notes.
Isolated initial backdrop behavior and independence from knockout.
Page group isolation, medium backdrop, default/output blending space and conversion intent.
Two CA/ca constants, AIS interpretation, nonstroking alpha also applied to group result.

errata: Primary annotation JSON confirms EC3 #345 on physical pp.407–408 (printed pp.392–393): Figures 72–73 are indicative, not pixel/color-precise; this does not affect formula-derived test oracles. EC3 #688 on physical p.428 (printed p.413) inserts Greek α in two §11.4.8 initialization symbols, correcting lowercase a_g0 and a_0 to α_g0 and α_0. `doc/errata-read.md` omits these assigned-section corrections, so the inventory-only search was incomplete.

ledger.evidence: Ledger cites render-cpu/tests/soft_mask.rs::a_constant_mask_interpolates_between_the_object_and_the_backdrop and describes a closed-form assertion. That assertion has an opaque backdrop and a Normal blend; it tests alpha interpolation, not arbitrary B(Cb,Cs) with both alphas nontrivial.

Many page/group color-space tests; selected route and profile tests exist. One-component source-to-blending-space conversion is explicitly a processor choice/residual in ledger note/ADR 0790, not ISO-mandated exact conversion.

Current separable_blend_oracle_audit.rs directly derives all twelve Table 134 outputs and has endpoint/piecewise controls; its named test also includes hand-derived Table 135 RGB values. These are opaque-fill tests, so mode function oracle quality is stronger than the full alpha+blend composition oracle.

Transparency and group tests cover alpha, shape, AIS, alpha constants, and transparent initial backdrop. Existing soft-mask alpha loop exercises Normal weighted compositing. This pass did not independently re-evaluate every source shape route (patterns/images/text/AA edges).

Numerous direct-pixel tests cover nonisolated/isolated group, knockout, page group/medium and blending-space paths. Reuse prior transparency_groups_current audit; this shard does not recertify every general group equation or backend.

Ledger references tests for CA/ca separate strokes/fills, opacity and shape/AIS controls; groups test group result alpha constant. This shard reviewed assertion presence and source semantics, not every operator consumer.

limitations: Test draft is unexecuted by this shard; parent must integrate/run it.
No claim that passing shared-backend comparisons independently verifies an ISO formula.
No exhaustive recalculation of group or page-group formulas; prior group shard is related context, not proof for all combinations.
No assessment of GPU unsupported-space policy or application-level renderer selection.
